clue.text: Star Wars movie fan cast Ewok here, somehow

indicators.note: somehow says the letters get there by some unstated route, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the fifteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A fan dressed up as an Ewok turns up at a Star Wars screening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; the signal is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Force Awakens (2015) is the seventh episode of the main Star Wars film saga.

clue.text: Loud cheers and mocking to welcome daughter

parts.note: ta and cheers both mean thanks in British slang

indicators.note: to welcome a guest is to take them inside

parts.note: wry means drily mocking
D abbreviates daughter

explanation.surface: Raucous cheering and jeering greet a daughter's arrival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loud' looks like noise, but here it means garish, as of clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud colours are showy and vulgar, and tawdry means cheaply gaudy.

clue.text: It's self-indulgent to produce tears after each of the main awards

indicators.note: after means placed following what comes next in the clue

parts.note: EGOT: winning an Emmy, Grammy, Oscar and Tony
rip and tear are synonyms

explanation.surface: A tearful winner sweeping every major showbiz award looks indulgent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tears' suggests weeping, but it is the verb, rips. EGOT is the showbiz term for winning all four major American awards.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is an activity done for self-gratification, a self-indulgent thing.

clue.text: Umpire's call sounded excessive

parts.note: a cricket umpire calls over after each set of six balls
as a horn or whistle is sounded

explanation.surface: An umpire's decision is said to have been far too harsh.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an over is six balls bowled from one end, ended by the umpire's call.
explanation.definitionFit: Overblown means inflated or exaggerated beyond what is warranted, hence excessive.

clue.text: Two-time champion's beginning to warm up

indicators.note: beginning points to the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter of champion
to heat is to warm up

explanation.surface: A double champion gets ready for the event by warming up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two-time' looks like a sporting record, but it is the verb meaning to be unfaithful.
explanation.definitionFit: To two-time a partner is to be unfaithful, which is to cheat on them.

clue.text: Caution mostly exercised, holding dull-looking gun

indicators.note: holding means keeping something inside
exercised suggests being worked and moved about
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
mat, or matt, describes a surface without shine

explanation.surface: Someone handles a dull grey gun with careful caution.
explanation.walkthrough: The dull-looking piece sits inside the shuffled letters rather than at either end, so the container comes after the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An automatic is a firearm that keeps firing as long as the trigger is held.

clue.text: 5 for the People, say, almost all worthless

indicators.note: almost means just short, so the final letter goes

parts.note: taken as written
bum is British slang for poor or worthless

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a record as almost entirely rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 refers to 5-down, AUTOMATIC: Automatic for the People is the 1992 R.E.M. record.
explanation.definitionFit: Automatic for the People is a record by R.E.M., an example of an LP release.

clue.text: Erected citadels in Europe, somewhat isolated

indicators.note: in a down clue, erected means stood upright, so read from bottom to top
somewhat means only part of the run of words is used

parts.note: inside the run of these three words

explanation.surface: Fortresses built around Europe stood somewhat apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Enisled is a poetic word meaning placed on an island, cut off, so isolated.

clue.text: Escape mounted under cover of school timetable

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means placed below the next word

parts.note: SCH abbreviates school

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means going upward, so read bottom to top

parts.note: to elude is to escape

explanation.surface: A pupil makes a break for it, climbing out under the school's cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A schedule is a plan listing times of events, a timetable.

clue.text: Everything with pickle

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for with
a pickle is a predicament, as is a hole

explanation.surface: Someone orders a dish with everything on it, pickle included.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole of something is all of it, every part included.

clue.text: No good to go for effort in English show

indicators.note: one thing going for another means it is swapped out and replaced

parts.note: N and G abbreviate no and good
a stab is an attempt or effort
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poor showing by the English side is put down to lack of effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No good' looks like a verdict on the team, but it is two abbreviations to remove from English.
explanation.definitionFit: To establish a fact is to show or prove that it is true.

clue.text: Dish's undercooked part

parts.note: meat cooked only lightly is rare
a bit is a part of something

explanation.surface: A diner complains that part of their dish is undercooked.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking dish to the wordplay. Welsh rarebit is cheese on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarebit, or Welsh rabbit, is a savoury dish of melted cheese sauce on toast.

clue.text: Old lady suffered and didn't speak up

parts.note: old lady is slang for one's mother
to bleed is to suffer, as in bleeding for a cause

explanation.surface: An elderly woman endured her troubles in silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who mumbles speaks indistinctly and too quietly, the opposite of speaking clearly and loudly.

clue.text: Work restricted without concerning them?

parts.note: OP abbreviates opus, a work

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: pent, as in pent up, means confined
on means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A work is restricted, but without saying who or what it concerns.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: the opponent is the 'them' in us versus them.
explanation.definitionFit: In a contest it is us against them, so an opponent is the other side, them.

clue.text: Thin person damaged chrome pot

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A skinny person has dented a shiny chrome pot.
explanation.definitionFit: An ectomorph is a body type that is lean and slight, a naturally slim build.

clue.text: Siegfried finally entering Ring cycle

indicators.note: entering means going inside another word

parts.note: a peal is a ring of bells

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the preceding word

parts.note: last letter of Siegfried

explanation.surface: The close of Siegfried leads into the rest of Wagner's Ring cycle.
explanation.walkthrough: Wagner's Ring cycle is a red herring: Ring is the wordplay and cycle the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To cycle is to ride a bicycle, which you do by pedalling it.

clue.text: Enter picture books into soup packet

indicators.note: into means going inside something

parts.note: pho is a Vietnamese noodle soup
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
packet and bomb are British slang for a large sum of money

explanation.surface: Someone puts books into a packet of soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cost a packet' and 'cost a bomb' both mean very expensive in British English.
explanation.definitionFit: To photobomb is to jump into someone else's photo uninvited, entering the picture.

clue.text: Exhausted student tackling new bit of maths

indicators.note: tackling means wrapping arms around and taking on

parts.note: a coed is a female student at a mixed college
N abbreviates new
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A weary student takes on a new piece of maths homework.
explanation.definitionFit: Something consumed has been used up entirely, so it is exhausted.

clue.text: Scotsman's no company for returning Indian, say

indicators.note: returning means heading back the way it came, so read backwards

parts.note: nae is Scots for no
CO abbreviates company

explanation.surface: A Scot won't keep company with an Indian visitor going home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian, say' means an example of what Indian might name: the Indian Ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian is one of the world's great oceans, so it is an example of the answer.

clue.text: Old tree likely to get hollowed out

parts.note: the elder is a tree

indicators.note: hollowed out means the inside is removed, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: outer letters of likely

explanation.surface: An ancient tree will probably end up hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderly describes people who are aged, in later life.

clue.text: Broadcast TV OK with Eric Idle

indicators.note: broadcast in its sense of scattered widely, as seed is sown

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Television executives approve a show starring Eric Idle of Monty Python.
explanation.walkthrough: Eric Idle is one of the Monty Python team; here Eric is fodder and Idle the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine that ticks over is running slowly without doing work, which is idling.

clue.text: Dictator engaged in river survey

indicators.note: engaged in means occupied inside

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
Idi Amin, the Ugandan dictator

explanation.surface: A dictator is busy with a survey of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To survey something is to look it over carefully, to inspect it closely.

clue.text: Meagre, filthy home's outside toilet

indicators.note: is outside means wrapping round the next item

parts.note: a pigsty is a filthy home
can is slang for toilet

explanation.surface: A poor, dirty house has its toilet out in the yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside toilet' reads as an outdoor loo, but outside is the instruction to wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Scanty means barely sufficient in amount, hence meagre.

clue.text: Type of card enclosing precious weapon

indicators.note: enclosing means wrapping around something else

parts.note: a SIM card in a mobile phone
dear means precious or beloved

explanation.surface: A treasured card holds a precious stone inside, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidearm is a small weapon such as a pistol worn at the side.

clue.text: I bail out?

indicators.note: out suggests being put out of order

parts.note: the five letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A suspect wonders whether to skip bail.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a good excuse is how I get out of trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere, which can get the accused off the hook.

clue.text: Boring spies with very standard way of talking back

indicators.note: back means everything before it is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency
so means very, as in so good
RP is Received Pronunciation, standard British English accent

explanation.surface: Dull spies speak in a very standard accent when they answer back.
explanation.walkthrough: Received Pronunciation is the traditional 'BBC' accent of southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosaic means dull and lacking imagination, so it is boring.

clue.text: Difficult question about bribe overturned

indicators.note: in a down clue, overturned means flipped upside down

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a sop is something given to placate, a bribe

explanation.surface: A tricky question arises about a bribe that was overturned.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is a puzzling question that is hard to answer.

clue.text: Millions hanging about to enjoy festival

parts.note: M abbreviates millions

indicators.note: about means placed around something else

parts.note: an arras is a tapestry wall hanging
to dig something is slang for liking it

explanation.surface: Millions of people hang about enjoying themselves at a carnival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hanging about' reads as loitering, but hanging is a noun here, the tapestry.
explanation.definitionFit: Mardi Gras is the Shrove Tuesday carnival, celebrated famously in New Orleans and Rio.

clue.text: Two legs, either side of one head

indicators.note: either side of means flanking something in the middle

parts.note: two of the cricket leg side, also called the on side
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A body with two legs on either side of a single head.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is also the on side, so leg gives ON. 'Use your onion' is old British slang for 'use your head'.
explanation.definitionFit: Onion is a dated British slang word for the head, as in 'off one's onion'.

clue.text: Extortion that might leave us in the dark?

definitions.text: that might leave us in the dark?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: stealing the light of day

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a whimsical literal reading of the idiom: if the daylight were stolen, we would be left in darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a price so outrageous that it amounts to open theft committed in broad day.
